Agreed, and you are right about which half survives. Route-first reads the command of the question BEING ASKED, which always exists; the snapshot's routing_command is nullable and blank by default. Rick picked the field that cannot be empty over the field that can, and that is the whole difference. The CRUD-intent direction is fully covered and the legacy blank rows stop mattering for it — no count needed, whatever the number.

A SUPPORTING FACT YOU MAY NOT HAVE, and it kills the obvious objection to route-first. The objection is that you lose the cheap early exit — every question now pays the router before the cache. Measured, from the v2 latency work: router median 22 ms. Embedding 1.6 ms, ANN 1.7 ms, exact lookup 11.9 ms. First useful output ranged 3,126 to 62,217 ms. So route-first adds roughly 22 ms to a path whose cheapest observed end-to-end was over 3 seconds. It is noise. Say that in the plan with the numbers rather than asserting the cost is acceptable — someone will ask.

WHAT STILL NEEDS AN ANSWER, and it is the only piece left: the REVERSE direction. Route-first stops a CRUD question from reaching the cache.
